selected_evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs on node1
selected_evidence.summary: /etc/cron.allow contains exactly root and opsadmin with root:root ownership and mode 0600. Effective checks show root and opsadmin reach their empty crontabs, while nobody receives an explicit access-denied response, both before and after restart.

Baseline boot ID was 9bdcc129-3d25-48ff-ad64-56be332fb91e with crond healthy. The safe reboot was acknowledged, and the post-restart boot ID changed to e0c3b037-bc49-48b9-ab9e-5b4416450ea4. After recovery, crond was active/enabled and the account, policy, and effective access behavior remained intact.

commands.command:
set -eu
if ! getent passwd opsadmin >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash opsadmin
  passwd -l opsadmin >/dev/null
fi
tmpfile=$(mktemp /etc/cron.allow.XXXXXX)
printf '%s\n' root opsadmin > "$tmpfile"
chown root:root "$tmpfile"
chmod 600 "$tmpfile"
mv -f "$tmpfile" /etc/cron.allow
printf '%s\n' '--- installed policy ---'
stat -c '%n %U:%G %a' /etc/cron.allow
cat /etc/cron.allow
printf '%s\n' '--- opsadmin account ---'
getent passwd opsadmin
passwd -S opsadmin
commands.stdout:
--- installed policy ---
/etc/cron.allow root:root 600
root
opsadmin
--- opsadmin account ---
opsadmin:x:1000:1000::/home/opsadmin:/bin/bash

commands.command:
set +e
check_user() {
  u=$1
  outfile=$(mktemp)
  if [ "$u" = root ]; then
    crontab -l >"$outfile" 2>&1
  else
    runuser -u "$u" -- crontab -l >"$outfile" 2>&1
  fi
  rc=$?
  printf 'user=%s rc=%s output=' "$u" "$rc"
  tr '\n' ' ' <"$outfile"
  printf '\n'
  rm -f "$outfile"
}
printf '%s\n' '--- policy content and metadata ---'
stat -c '%n %U:%G %a' /etc/cron.allow
cat /etc/cron.allow
printf '%s\n' '--- effective crontab access ---'
check_user root
check_user opsadmin
check_user nobody
printf '%s\n' '--- service health ---'
systemctl is-active crond
systemctl is-enabled crond
systemctl --no-pager --full status crond | sed -n '1,8p'
exit 0
